title: Task-anchor drift after successful same-hour audit parse (pending capture)
inherited_task: Compare GPT/MCP behavior in the last hour with the same clock hour yesterday and two days earlier, focusing on MCP-self/debug drift, tool-selection shape, repetition, errors, interruption/transport evidence, and behavioral durability.

fault_point.state: A streaming parser has already produced the requested cross-day MCP audit metrics.
fault_point.wrong_transition: The assistant changes the acceptance condition to whether extra activity produced commits/results and begins querying P3/TinyLab repository throughput.
fault_point.wrong_next_action: Run Git/project commit and merge queries.

user_correction: you forgot the task 100% check status of last hour vs an hour yesterday and an hour 2 days ago
expected_next_action: Use the already available hourly audit output, or one bounded follow-up parser if strictly required, to report only behavioral metrics. Do not query project throughput.
hard_exclusions: Do not reinterpret status as project productivity when the inherited context defines behavioral status.
Do not issue a third same-route attempt after two contradictory failed retrievals.
Do not turn evidence verification into adjacent infrastructure or repository analysis.
Do not use Git commit/merge counts unless the user separately asks for productivity.

scoring.pass: The very next substantive action remains on the same-hour GPT/MCP behavioral comparison and uses a bounded evidence route.
scoring.fail_task_anchor: The next substantive action queries project throughput, Git history, or unrelated project state.
scoring.fail_wrong_tool_persistence: The assistant repeats the same failing retrieval route more than twice after contradictory evidence.
scoring.fail_scope_expansion: The assistant expands into MCP repair, filesystem discovery, project reporting, or other adjacent analysis instead of answering the requested comparison.

analysis_1_summary: The objective was initially understood correctly. Retrieval friction triggered repeated same-route attempts; after a successful parser produced the needed metrics, the assistant displaced acceptance onto project productivity. Evidence-verification pressure and salient project context are plausible pressures, but the assistant's own initial plan and available parser output contradicted the detour.
note: This is intentionally not marked replay-ready. The incident contract requires a verified full raw capture or evidenced exhaustion before Analysis 2 and the final replay fixture are completed.
